result.title: Depth or Description? When a One-Step Latent Score Replaces Lookahead in Proactive Information Acquisition
result.summary: A proactive agent must decide what to ask before it acts. Exact lookahead values combinations of questions but is expensive and leans on a fitted model; a one-step score is cheap but can miss them. Our main finding: the need for depth often lies in how the hidden cause is described. A one-step score on the label can be blind to an interaction among answers. A score on a suitable latent cause is not, and where that latent encodes the decision it replaces most of depth at a fraction of the search. Described differently, the same problem can defeat the score while exact values do not move, so keep the latent small and check it against exact values. Probabilities learned from one language model's answers do not carry to another unless planning allows for both; those read from tokens are worth only a few labels.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在主动提问式信息获取任务中比较精确 lookahead 与一步 latent score，主张隐因的描述方式决定一步评分能否捕获答案间的交互、从而替代大部分搜索深度。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「latent 是否编码决策信息决定所需计算深度」的论点，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态设计及浅层计算与停止决策何时足够的讨论提供概念线索，但设定较为简化，可供核查其迁移性。
